name: Lagoon Nebula
tagline: A stellar nursery the naked eye can see — the great star-forming pool of Sagittarius.
history: The Lagoon Nebula is one of only two star-forming clouds bright enough to see naked-eye — a 110-light-year pool of pink hydrogen gas where the open cluster NGC 6530 is already hatched and sculpting the remaining material into pillars, globules and the brilliant 'Hourglass' knot at its heart. It is Orion's grander southern cousin, a full stellar nursery caught mid-work on the edge of our galactic view toward the center.
